usa.title: Indonesia's VP resigns as his eligibility and academic credentials are questioned

usa.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang steps down amid alleged spy scandal

usa.title: At least 23 states considered laws governing ICE and schools this year

usa.title: Brooklyn building collapse death toll rises to 8 as rescuers search for survivors

usa.title: Sharp swings for Nvidia and oil prices weigh on Wall Street

usa.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after his affair raises national security concerns

usa.title: Indictment sheds light on alleged Iran-backed plots across U.S. and Europe
usa.summary: Iran's top national security official warned that it would strike American bases beyond the Gulf, including in Europe, if the United States resumes air strikes against the Islamic Republic. The warning comes one day after indictments in New York against three men who allegedly conspired to attack U.S. Air Force planes at a base in England. Nick Schifrin reports.

usa.title: News Wrap: Democrat Scott Colom defeats Mississippi Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith
usa.summary: In our news wrap Wednesday, Democrat Scott Colom has defeated incumbent Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi, a group that included Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth was admonished by an Army sentinel at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier and peace talks between Ukraine, Russia and the U.S. ended with an agreement to exchange prisoners, but no breakthrough on ending the war.

usa.title: White House threatens Democrats over plans to investigate Trump officials
usa.summary: With Democrats set to take control of Congress, the White House is threatening them over investigations into the Trump administration. The top White House lawyer warned that aggressive oversight of the administration "may cross the line into blatant criminality." It comes amid a wave of resignations within the Justice Department. Amna Nawaz discussed more with Devlin Barrett of The New York Times.

usa.title: Sen. Coons on Huang affair, Iran war and why Trump should fire Hegseth
usa.summary: As Democrats prepare to take control of Congress, Delaware Sen. Chris Coons is poised to become chairman of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, succeeding retiring Democrat Jeanne Shaheen. A staunch supporter of Ukraine and a critic of President Trump's war with Iran, Coons would take the helm at a consequential moment for American foreign policy.  Coons joined Geoff Bennett to discuss more.

usa.title: How companies are using AI to make you spend more money
usa.summary: Companies have always tried to maximize profits, but now there are a host of sophisticated tools to determine the prices of the goods and services they sell. At a time when so many Americans are frustrated with rising costs, those tools are under greater scrutiny. Economics correspondent Paul Solman explains how that technology is transforming the prices we pay.

usa.title: How America's military shaped the nation's history and evolved over 250 years
usa.summary: Over the last 250 years, the United States military has helped shape the nation's history – from the fight for independence to its emergence as the world's leading military power. But as the military's reach has grown, fewer Americans are serving in uniform. Judy Woodruff explores what that means for the country in her series, Crossroads: America at 250.

usa.title: New film 'The Mosquito Bowl' tells story of WWII football game between Marines
